title: Browser tree: each setup owns its WCS, Stock, Machine, Post, Fixtures and Tool list

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Requested by the maintainer (2026-11-08): "The 'Machine', 'Post' should have their own sections in the browser tree under its selected setup. Instead of living under 'stock', 'Fixture' and 'Tool list' should live in the browser under respective setup as well.. As they are setup specific, and editable."

## Today (main)
- `SetupDef` stores `stock`, `wcs`, `datum_from`, `work_offset` - **no machine and no post**: both are document-wide.
- Fixtures already bind to a setup (`FixtureDef.setup`), but the browser shows them under Stock.
- Tools are a document-wide list in a top-level **Tools** browser section; the per-setup tool list exists only as a derived view (setup sheet / Setups page).
- Machine and Post are reached from the ribbon, not the tree.

## What it should be
Each setup in the browser is a node with its own editable children, in this order:

```
Setup1
  WCS            (one per setup - #342; label G54..G59 set on the setup)
  Stock
  Machine        (the setup's machine file)
  Post           (the setup's post processor + its options)
  Fixtures       (the setup's workholding, each fixture a child)
  Tool list      (the tools this setup's operations use, editable)
  Operations     (1+n ops, in machining order)
Setup2
  ...
```

Clicking a node opens its editor (the existing Stock / Machine / Post / Tools pages scoped to that setup); every edit stays an undoable command.

## Per-node behaviour (maintainer, 2026-11-08 - issue comment)
- **Setup selection:** the active setup is chosen with a **radio button** on each setup node in the browser tree (one active at a time; `ActivateSetup`, undoable).
- **Clicking a setup** opens its settings in the right pane, including the **stock source**: use its own stock, or inherit the machined stock from the previous setup in the tree (#317/#320). The first setup has no inherit option.
- **WCS:** opens a right-pane dialog for setting the setup's WCS (origin, 3-2-1 / numeric) and its name, the post label **G54-G59** (#342: one WCS per setup; the label is what the post writes).
- **Stock:** as it is today.
- **Machine:** opens the machine selector in the right pane (for now).
- **Post:** opens the post selector in the right pane (for now).
- **Fixtures:** loading and positioning fixtures for this setup.
- **Tool list:** opens a right-pane dialog with a table of the tools added to this setup and the tool-list export.
- **Operations:** as now - a 1+n tree of the setup's operations; clicking one opens its dialog in the right pane.

## Model changes this needs
- **Machine and Post per setup:** add them to the setup (default: the document's current machine/post, so existing files load and post byte-identically). Two setups may use different machines/posts (e.g. a mill then a lathe). Posting a program that spans setups with different posts writes one file per post (or refuses by name - decide and record).
- **Tool list per setup:** decide between (a) a per-setup tool library (tools copied/assigned per setup) and (b) the document library with a per-setup filtered, editable view (editing a tool edits it everywhere it is used - must say so). Record the decision; keep tool numbers unique per setup's program.
- **Fixtures:** move from under Stock to the setup's own Fixtures node (no model change - `FixtureDef.setup` already exists).
- Project file version bump; old files: every setup takes the document's machine/post; fixtures keep their binding.

## Done means
The tree shows the per-setup structure above; each node opens its scoped editor; machine and post are stored per setup with the migration above; fixtures and tool list appear under their setup; undo/redo for every edit; posting stays byte-identical for single-setup documents; UI tests for the tree structure and node actions; shell snapshots regenerated.

Related: #342 (one WCS per setup), #45 (setup navigation / op ordering in the browser), #148 and #287 (machine editor / machines pane), #322 (Setups reachable), #308 (multi-setup chain).
